task1.prompt: The line graph below shows the average number of commuters, in thousands, who used three different modes of transport on a typical weekday in one city between 1990 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Daily commuters by mode of transport (thousands)

task1.sample:
The line graph illustrates how many commuters, in thousands, used buses, trains and bicycles on an average weekday in one city between 1990 and 2020.

Overall, the number of train and bicycle users increased substantially, whereas bus ridership stayed fairly stable with only minor fluctuations. Cycling, which started from a very low base, showed the most dramatic growth.

In 1990, buses were by far the most popular option, carrying 120,000 passengers, twice as many as trains (60,000) and far ahead of bicycles, which attracted a mere 5,000 commuters. Over the following fifteen years, bus use fell gradually to 100,000, while train travel rose steadily and had overtaken it by 2005, at 110,000.

From 2005 onwards, trains continued to gain passengers, peaking at 145,000 in 2015 before easing to 135,000 in 2020. Bus usage bottomed out at 98,000 in 2010 and then recovered to 125,000, finishing slightly above its original level. Meanwhile, cycling grew at an accelerating pace, from 20,000 in 2005 to 78,000 in 2020, a more than fifteen-fold increase on the 1990 figure.
task1.notes_vi: Biểu đồ đường: tập trung vào XU HƯỚNG và điểm giao nhau. Dàn ý: Mở bài paraphrase; Overview nêu xu hướng chung (tàu và xe đạp tăng, xe buýt gần như ổn định, xe đạp tăng nhanh nhất); Thân bài 1: giai đoạn 1990–2005 (xe buýt giảm, tàu vượt xe buýt); Thân bài 2: 2005–2020 (đỉnh, đáy, mức cuối). Từ vựng: rise steadily, climb, peak at, bottom out at, overtake, fluctuate, a more than fifteen-fold increase. Lỗi hay gặp: mô tả từng năm một thay vì nhóm số liệu; không nhắc điểm giao nhau giữa các đường; nhầm 'number' và 'proportion'; quên đơn vị (thousands) nên sai mức số; dùng 'increase' lặp lại quá nhiều.

task2.prompt: Some people think that university students should study subjects that will help them find a job, while others believe they should choose subjects they enjoy. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
task2.sample:
The question of how students should choose their university subjects divides opinion. Some people argue that employability ought to be the main consideration, whereas others maintain that personal interest matters more. In my view, both factors are important, but passion should carry slightly greater weight.

Those who advocate career-focused degrees point to the financial pressures that graduates face. Tuition fees and living costs mean that many students leave university with substantial debts, so a qualification in a field with strong demand, such as engineering, nursing or data analysis, offers a clearer route to a stable income. Furthermore, parents who have invested in their children's education understandably want to see a tangible return. In a competitive job market, a degree with obvious professional value can make the difference between finding work quickly and struggling for years.

On the other hand, there are compelling reasons to follow one's interests. Students who enjoy their subject tend to be more motivated, attend classes more regularly and achieve better results, which in turn improves their prospects. Moreover, the job market changes rapidly. A skill that is in high demand today may be automated or oversupplied in a decade, whereas curiosity and the ability to learn deeply are qualities that remain valuable in any career. Many successful people, such as writers or entrepreneurs, have built careers that bear little relation to their original degrees.

Personally, I believe the best approach is to seek a balance. Students should research the job prospects of the subjects they are considering, but they should not choose a course they dislike simply because it pays well. Someone who is genuinely engaged will usually find a way to turn that enthusiasm into employment, perhaps by combining their main subject with practical modules or internships.

In conclusion, although career considerations are understandable, I think students are likely to be happier and more successful if their choice is driven primarily by interest, supported by realistic planning.
task2.notes_vi: Dạng Discussion (both views) + opinion: PHẢI bàn cả hai quan điểm và nêu ý kiến riêng. Dàn ý: Mở bài (paraphrase + nói sẽ thảo luận hai phía + ý kiến sơ bộ) — Thân bài 1: quan điểm thứ nhất (chọn ngành dễ xin việc) với 1–2 lý do — Thân bài 2: quan điểm thứ hai (chọn ngành yêu thích) — đoạn thân bài hoặc kết bài nêu rõ ý kiến cá nhân — Kết bài. Lỗi hay gặp: chỉ bàn một phía; không nêu ý kiến riêng (mất điểm Task Response); liệt kê ý mà không giải thích 'vì sao'; dùng 'firstly, secondly' máy móc; dùng từ nối sai như 'On the contrary' khi chỉ cần 'On the other hand'; ý kiến đưa ra ở kết bài khác với mở bài.
